sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?composer 
 WHERE {
 ?composer rdf:type mo:MusicArtist .
 ?composer foaf:name "%s" .
 ?tune rdf:type mo:MusicalWork .
 ?tune dtl:composed_by ?composer .
 }
gold_question: Is there more than one composer with this name in the graph?

model_output.nl_question: Which musician with the given name is the composer of at least one musical work?
model_output.confidence_rationale: There is no direct NL evidence matching the query intent. The question is inferred from the SPARQL structure, which selects a MusicArtist with the given name who is linked via composed_by to a MusicalWork. The mapping is straightforward but lacks supporting textual evidence.

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?arranger 
 WHERE {
 ?arranger rdf:type mo:MusicArtist .
 ?arranger foaf:name "%s" .
 ?tune rdf:type mo:MusicalWork .
 ?tune dtl:arranged_by ?arranger .
 }
gold_question: Is there more than one arranger with this name in the graph?

review.note: This could be name disambiguation on the one hand - is there more than one arranger with this name in the dataset. Or, on the other hand, it could be a check whether there is an arranger with this name (this is what was generated), or whether this musician did any arrangements. The presence of 'distinct' suggests the former I would say.

model_output.nl_question: Which musician with the given name has arranged at least one musical work?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The question is derived directly from the SPARQL structure: it selects a MusicArtist (by name) who is linked via arranged_by to at least one MusicalWork. No provided NL evidence mentions arranging, so confidence is reduced.

sparql:

PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
SELECT ?trackt ?signal
 WHERE {
 ?track rdf:type mo:Track .
 ?track dc:title ?trackt .
 ?track mo:track_number "%i" .
 ?medium mo:track ?track .
 ?medium dc:title ?mediumt .
 ?medium mo:record_number "%i" .
 ?release mo:record ?medium .
 ?release dc:title "%s" .
 ?signal mo:published_as ?track .
 }
gold_question: Given the album title, disk number and track number, find the track title and the associated signal

review.note: My main concern here is the album vs release difference - in NL we would talk about album title rather than release title; in the ontology, release was chosen rather than album to indicate the relation to time

model_output.nl_question: Given a release title, a record number, and a track number, what is the track’s title and which audio signal was published as that track?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The SPARQL clearly selects a track by its track number within a specific record (by record number) on a given release (by title) and returns the track title plus the signal linked via mo:published_as. Ontology and graph-shape evidence support the property chain and the Signal→Track relation, but there is no direct NL competency question matching this query.

}

review.note:
This is too detailed for NL even though it is more exact then previously

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX event: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/event.owl#>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX tl: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/timeline.owl#>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT ?bandname ?performance_title ?startdate
?solostart ?solo_instrument_label ?soloist_name
WHERE {
?performance rdf:type mo:Performance .
?performance dc:title ?performance_title .
?session event:sub_event ?performance .
?session event:time ?date .
?date tl:at ?startdate .
?session mo:performer ?band .
?band foaf:name ?bandname .
?performance event:sub_event ?solo .
?solo event:time ?solotime .
?solotime tl:beginsAt ?solostart .
?solotime tl:endsAt ?soloend .
?solo dtl:solo_instrument ?solo_instrument .
?solo_instrument dtl:dtl_inst_label
?solo_instrument_label .
?solo dtl:solo_performer ?soloperformer .
?soloperformer dtl:musician ?soloist .
?soloist foaf:name ?soloist_name .
}
gold_question: List all solos with attributed solo performers, with the track title and date, solo timestamp and instrument

review.note: This generated version lost the soloist, which is important because not solos have soloists attributed to them

model_output.nl_question: Which performances include solos, and for each solo what is the start time, the soloist, and the instrument, along with the performance title, band name, and date?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The SPARQL lists performances within sessions and, for each solo, returns the start time, the soloist, and the instrument label, plus performance title, band name, and date. CQ6 covers solos with timestamps, and CQ7 covers solos with attributed musicians; CQ9 supports the instruments aspect. This closely matches the query’s intent.

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX event: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/event.owl#>

PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT ?bandname ?performance_title ?solodate
?solostart ?soloend
WHERE {
?performance rdf:type mo:Performance .
?performance dc:title ?performance_title .
?session event:sub_event ?performance .
?session event:time ?date .
?date tl:at ?solodate .
?session mo:performer ?band .
?band foaf:name ?bandname .
?performance event:sub_event ?solo .
?solo event:time ?solotime .
?solotime tl:beginsAt ?solostart .
?solotime tl:endsAt ?soloend .
?solo dtl:solo_performer ?soloperformer .
?soloperformer dtl:musician ?soloist .
?soloist foaf:name "Dizzy Gillespie" .
FILTER (YEAR(?solodate) < 1950)}
ORDER BY (?solodate)

model_output.confidence_rationale: CQ8 directly matches the query’s core intent (solos by a specific musician over a time period). CQ6 supports inclusion of solo timestamps, which the query returns. The alignment is strong and specific to the SPARQL constraints.
